page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.ce4.xlarge in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, including stress-ng and Geekbench, rank in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large-block read operations scoring in the bottom 10% at 22.44 GB/sec, and large-block write operations in the bottom 25% at 14.99 GB/sec. However, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, and text generation using a small 135M LLM model achieves an average speed of 80.49 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.ce4.xlarge is its reliance on older Intel Broadwell architecture, which limits its computational throughput and memory speed compared to modern hardware generations. Qualitatively, it offers a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated physical cores and a high memory footprint without the premium price of newer architectures. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive but computationally moderate workloads, such as caching layers, small database operations, and basic web serving.
